note: Primary rootCause per event plus contributingFactors drawn from the same codes. Mechanism = the recurring causal pattern, not the incident.

RC-GOV-UNTESTED.name: Governance/verification artefact first exercised in the timed run
RC-GOV-UNTESTED.mechanism: Gates, frozen plans, suite commands, approval formats and contracts were validated only against synthetic fixtures (or not at all) before T0, so their defects surface as refusals, deadlocks or unverifiable evidence inside the 420-minute window.
examples: CAUSA T18<->T20 cycle and process rules bound to R10 repo

RC-SELF-ATTEST.name: Agent-stated status exceeds evidence
RC-SELF-ATTEST.mechanism: The implementing agent reports acceptance, coverage, approvals or test existence that the primary evidence does not support; only independent review or computed verdicts catch it.

RC-DERIV-LOSS.name: Requirement loss during derivation
RC-DERIV-LOSS.mechanism: Compression of a large baseline into a smaller criteria set silently drops mandatory obligations; no gate compared derivation with source.

RC-PROVIDER-MODEL.name: Fake provider diverges from real provider
RC-PROVIDER-MODEL.mechanism: Test doubles do not model real GitHub semantics (status codes, caching, races, rate limits, data contract), so defects appear only in live runs or reviews.

RC-CONCURRENCY.name: Multi-writer / identity / stale-state persistence semantics
RC-CONCURRENCY.mechanism: Save confirmation, request identity and cross-tab state are designed per instance; the same invariants (DC-001..006, AR-035) are re-violated in each fresh implementation.

RC-FIX-REGRESSION.name: Fix-induced defect or instance-level fix of a class
RC-FIX-REGRESSION.mechanism: A correction is checked only against the reported instance, not against every consumer or variant, so a new defect or the same class recurs.

RC-CI-HARNESS.name: CI pipeline configuration defect
RC-CI-HARNESS.mechanism: Workflow semantics (pipefail, concurrency groups, if: always(), job time limits, shared ports/test repos, SDK pins) make CI unable to fail, unable to finish, or flaky.

RC-ENV-SANDBOX.name: Execution-environment limit
RC-ENV-SANDBOX.mechanism: Session proxy, blocked registries, anonymous browser egress, permission guards and container restarts prevent local reproduction or credentialed checks.

RC-TOOLCHAIN.name: Upstream tool/runtime/SDK defect
RC-TOOLCHAIN.mechanism: Defects in Conditor, Praxis, Dokimos, the .NET WASM interpreter or SDK are hit by the rehearsal and fixed locally or upstream, sometimes repeatedly.

RC-STACK-SCOPE.name: Dependency outside the approved release set
RC-STACK-SCOPE.mechanism: A needed package is not in the locked set; only an owner re-pin can admit it.

RC-PARALLEL-WRITE.name: Parallel lanes write the same files
RC-PARALLEL-WRITE.mechanism: Several agents edit shared source or shared governance state (.ros) without machine-checked ownership; conflicts surface at merge time.

RC-OWNER-PREREQ.name: Owner-only prerequisite not ready before T0
RC-OWNER-PREREQ.mechanism: Secrets, Pages, rulesets, approvals and decisions only the owner can provide are missing at kickoff or attested in chat, consuming window time and leaving process obligations unverifiable.

RC-TIME-MGMT.name: Clock or merge-timing error
RC-TIME-MGMT.mechanism: Agents project time instead of reading the clock, leave green work unmerged, or merge while gates run.

RC-SECURITY-EXPOSURE.name: Secret or test-control exposure
RC-SECURITY-EXPOSURE.mechanism: Tokens reach artifacts/traces, test hooks reach production, read tokens can write.

RC-UI-SPEC.name: UI / design-token defect
RC-UI-SPEC.mechanism: Visual and accessibility defects not caught by bound tests (missing tokens, contrast, phone layout).

RC-PROVENANCE.name: Not built from requirements alone / cross-run evidence
RC-PROVENANCE.mechanism: Prior rehearsal code or evidence is reused, confounding comparison and invalidating closures.
